title: Choose Reglet’s visual world
question: Reglet needs a precise operating surface for comparing canonical artifacts with provider projections. Keep the calibration workbench, take a challenger, or re-roll.

options.label: Calibration Workbench
options.lineage: metrology labs, inspection cards, reference standards
options.thesis: Reglet is the reference standard that makes provider drift measurable before anything is applied.
options.viewport: A calm instrument bench: library index at left, selected artifact on the inspection bed, and a calibrated projection rail showing desired, applied, and observed state.
options.risk: The reference-instrument language becomes sterile if paper, annotation, and editorial hierarchy are underplayed.
options.case: Wins on product clarity: canonical reference, tolerance, drift, and explicit calibration map directly to Reglet’s core loop.

options.label: Creator Hardware
options.lineage: creator control surfaces and bench instruments
options.thesis: Every operation has tactile certainty, and the one safety-orange key commits an apply.
options.viewport: A strict key-grid workbench with grouped artifact functions, one orange Apply key, and a compact amber projection readout.
options.risk: A literal control panel can make nuanced artifact comparison feel like a collection of buttons.
options.case: Audience identification is excellent; it loses narrowly because ownership and scope are less legible than on the calibration bench.

options.label: Crew Terminal
options.thesis: Provider configuration becomes a shipboard system query with unmistakable hazards and acknowledgements.
options.viewport: A phosphor terminal answers a selected artifact query while hazard plates identify drift, missing secrets, and shadowed projections.
options.risk: The theatrical command-line topology can slow routine editing and comparison.
options.case: Fuses poorly because query-by-query navigation hides the simultaneous provider state Reglet must make obvious.

options.label: Drawcord Projection
options.thesis: One canonical plane gathers into several provider-specific shapes through visible constraints.
options.viewport: The canonical artifact is a flat pattern at center; provider outputs gather around it, connected by scope and compatibility channels.
options.risk: The transformation is memorable, but dense editing and exact state labels fight the textile metaphor.
options.case: Product transformation is clear, but audience identification and daily-operating precision are weaker.

canonCard.label: Conventional developer app
canonCard.lineage: desktop settings tools and modern admin consoles
canonCard.thesis: A familiar sidebar, table, editor, and details panel executed with exceptional restraint.
canonCard.viewport: Navigation sidebar, searchable artifact table, editor panel, and a conventional provider-status drawer.
canonCard.risk: Immediately usable, but visually interchangeable with other developer settings products.
